THE CONNECTED CONSUMER

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
There is a new breed of consumers – they know what they want and in are in complete control of their buying journey – meet the Connected Consumer.

Summary:
Consumers are digitally savvy than ever before – choosing the cyber space market over crowded malls. We meet two online shoppers and speak to an expert to discover the evolution of the path to purchases.

Further information:
Today, with the rise of the mobile connected consumer, the growing penetration of new technologies and a purchasing process reinvented through social collaboration, retailers face a more challenging, complex market space than ever before.
These consumers have been called - Generation C. Multitasking and multiscreen, always on, engaged in a cross-platform way, mobile, predominantly female, connected, different and empowered.

BUT WHAT INFLUENCES THEIR BUYING POWER?
Reviews, blogs, recommendations.

DIGITAL MARKETING expert Gillian Meier helps us understand the Connected Consumer and the cyber space market place they operate in.

Our two shoppers are:
LAURIE – 28 – works in social media marketing

- Regularly shops online – mostly for her spoils – not essentials – so work clothes, shoes home ware
- HATES shopping centres
- Find she spends more because it’s so easy – not physically holding the stuff, so no reasoning or magnitude of the purchase.
- Gets sucked into specials, deals and discounts – spends even more! APPs send constant deals – and once you look at 25% off stuff, you then see spending 500 bucks will get you 100 off – so you click add to cart, add to cart
- Also looks at reviews – not just the first 3 – but will look at 10 – and then decide what the average rating was – helps her suss out scams, looks at credibility.
- She regularly rates things – people should know – often we just complain, but the good service stories also need to get out

MONICA – 25 – works for a digital PR company

- Regularly shops online – mostly for clothes and accessories
- It’s a craze in her office – everyone shops online – they get so excited talking about their purchases. And when your box comes it’s like XMAS – and everyone wants to know what you got.
- Relies on reviews to help make decisions in the cyber shopping world.

Press Release:


The Connected Consumer
Are you part of ‘Generation C’? These digitally savvy consumers multitask on multiple screens, for instant buyer gratification and ditch over-crowded malls in favour of cyber space. Carte Blanche asks—what drives the rise of the connected consumer?


Script:


ONLINE SHOPPING

VO: The Inter-connectivity of apps and multiplatform devices takes the slog out of shopping - delivering the goods in just a few clicks.

LINK: There’s a new breed of consumer – they are smart, savvy and digitally connected on multiple platforms – they know what they want and where they are going to get it.

LAURIE: The less time I can spend in a shopping centre, the better.

SCENE: SHOP SHOP SHOP
VO: Online shopping has revolutionized 28 year old, Accounts Manager, Laurie Bauer’s life.

LAURIE: To just generally wait in queue, I feel like it’s a waste of life. // I could probably get more shopping done in the queue while I wait to pay for my goods.

VO: 25 year old Monica Mtshemla, is a social media manager – she says online shopping is next level convenience after the daily grind.

MONICA: The fact that I can do it while I’m sitting down, (laughs). PJS, Slippers, cup of tea with my doek on – it’s so convenient – I just really like it.

VO: While online shopping is a growing trend globally. It ONLY makes up 1% of South Africa’s Retail Spend.

The majority of shoppers still want to splurge with the masses.
VOX POP1
VOX POP2
VOX POP3

VO: Online Marketing Analyst Gillian Meier, says even if you are still buying offline, it’s likely that you’ve done cyber research.

GILLIAN: 60%....

VO: While Moinca admits, she does more research than online checkouts – she says, it helps focus her real life shopping expeditions.

MONICA: I would drive out to the stores where I would know I would find the items – so from Fourways, drive to Rosebank or drive to Sandton. So it save a lot of time and petrol.

VO: 41% of purchased item are not planned. Laurie showed us just how easy it is to get sucked into a shopper’s rabbit hole….

LAURIE: If you sign up with the newsletter, you get a R100 off – so that’s rad – so if you buy xyz – you get free delivery, then you get a R100 off and you just kind of justifying to yourself why you’re spending money.
LAURIE: oh my goodness! There is a sale! Actually lets go straight to the sales…
DEVI: you are a problem… I’ve only bought essentials, but it’s like you’ve opened up a whole new world.
DEVI: I can see why this can be so addictive….

VO: The convenience is undeniable, and retailers are constantly finding ways to improve online customer experiences in the hopes of securing more sales.

GILLIAN: The safety factor has definitely shifted where online stores are going out of their way to make it a safe environment for them.

VO: But online shops are getting smarter & more organised - using technology to lure shoppers and secure checkouts.

LAURIE: You’ve just been online looking at shoes and then you see it on your facebook account, no, no, I mustn’t, but they found me and they keep finding you over and over and you start getting stalked and you start feeling like it is sign.

VO: The so-called sign, is actually, online tracking technology.

GILLIAN: We call them very sticky clicks. They track a consumer – that brand follows you and keeps reminding you that you haven’t checked out your shopping cart. That is a very powerful way to get conversions.

DEVI: It calls for willpower
MONICA: It really does, I can’t tell you how much willpower I had to exercise in order not to spend more than that R1500 – that was my cut off mark – I was just like, I know you want more, I know you want this skirt, I know… but no!
LAURIE: I think if you’re in the shops, you see the volume – like you see what you have in your arms, and you’re like. But when you’re online you just see boxes – you’re just ticking boxes
DEVI: Ok, so the tough question – do you think you have a problem?
LAURIE: (laughs) I did have a problem – I really did – until about a month ago – I started cutting it down. I started to leave my credit card at home. I work in an office full of women and it’s also the kind of environment where you psyche each other up and then when you get the box – everyone is excited to see it.

VO: Gillian says in the digital world, connected consumers have no secrets. 26% of shoppers go online after getting their goods to either:
- share their purchase experience on social networks
- look for help on product usage
- or to post reviews or ratings about the buy.

GILLIAN: When they’ve had a good experience – they want to share it with somebody, when they’ve had a bad experience – they want to share it with everybody. And they do so instantly, no matter where they are that passion is often very honest, it’s authentic and it’s often very brutal.

VO: While the cyber market space is not one brands can ignore, traditional stores aren’t disappearing any time soon.


PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Meet the Connected Consumer – a new breed of online shoppers, who get what they want – whenever they want it in a couple of clicks.

LAURIE: To just generally wait in queue, I feel like it’s a waste of life. //

PROMO 2
VO: Digitally savvy consumers ditch over-crowded malls in favour of cyber space and instant gratification.

MONICA: PJS, Slippers, cup of tea with my doek on – it’s so convenient – I just really like it. INT3 M5


PROMO 3
VO: whether you’re buying online or in store – most purchases starts in cyber space.

GILLIAN: 60%....

VO: We explore the world of connected consumers.
